items.feedback_item: Daily solar balance claimed as 13.5 kWh per day yield covering 13.2 kWh per day load with 0.3 kWh per day margin is inconsistent because the load omits door loss.
items.must_change: The solution claimed grown-array daily yield of 13.5 kWh per day (E83) covers steady plus staged load of 13.2 kWh per day (E58) with margin of 0.3 kWh per day (E86), but what is actually true is the 13.2 kWh per day calculation using 203 W conduction (E41) plus fans plus controls plus 6.2 kWh staged pull-down omits the door infiltration of 0.44 kWh per day (E57), so the consistent total is about 13.7 kWh per day and exceeds yield by the relation yield equals peak kW times peak sun hours times derate and load equals steady times 24 plus pull-down plus door. The energy table and constraint table must be changed to add the door term, recompute required peak of about 3.52 kWp (E82) upward, and either grow the split array beyond 3.60 kWp or reduce steady and opening load to restore a usable positive margin, because otherwise the box does not hold 5C through the design day at 43C ambient.

items.feedback_item: Thermal watts were equated directly to electrical yield with no COP conversion for vapor compression.
items.must_change: The solution compared conduction of 203 W (E41) plus pull-down heat of 6.25 kWh staged and 25 kWh full-tonne (E28, E26) directly against electrical yield of 13.5 kWh per day (E83), but what is actually true is vapor compression requires electrical equals thermal divided by COP at 43C condenser conditions, and omitting COP uses the wrong model regime though the error is conservative when COP is above 1. The key estimates and measurement of load must be changed to state design COP at 43C ambient, convert all thermal kWh to electrical kWh, then resize array and battery from electrical load, because without this the panel and battery sizes do not prove autonomy.

items.feedback_item: Two different daily energies are claimed for the same staged duty and the balance is unsettled.
items.must_change: The solution claims steady plus staged load of 13.2 kWh per day (E58) and also staged-average of 615 W (E28), but what is actually true is 615 W times 24 divided by 1000 equals 14.8 kWh per day which contradicts 13.2 kWh per day by 1.6 kWh per day and leaves the balance unknown. The estimates must be changed to adopt one consistent conduction plus door plus fan plus pull-down summation with stated COP, remove the contradictory average, and reclose yield minus load, because the release margin cannot be judged until one number controls.

items.feedback_item: Door infiltration is shown with two values and the smaller value was used to preserve margin.
items.must_change: The solution shows door infiltration as 0.44 kWh per day sensible air only from 4 air changes times 8.64 m3 volume (E39) times 0.335 times 38 K divided by 1000 (E57) and also as 70 W average or 1.68 kWh per day inside the simulation (E28), but what is actually true is the larger value includes more openings and latent load and erases the 0.3 kWh per day margin (E86). The design must be changed to select one defensible door model tied to 8 daytime single-crate openings with strip curtain, include sensible plus latent, and carry that value through the daily total, because door discipline at 43C ambient decides whether staged 250 kg per day in 12.5 crates (E78) holds temperature.

items.feedback_item: Battery autonomy for night and cloudy-day operation was not sized.
items.must_change: The solution provides a battery bank with controller to store energy for night and cloud but gives no usable kWh, depth of discharge, inverter surge for monoblock start, or one-cloudy-day autonomy, while night load must be carried every night and any cloud breaks the 2 percent margin. The concept and constraint table must be changed to add battery usable kWh equals night electrical load divided by depth of discharge with efficiency, state days of autonomy, and show charge controller and shed logic from return-air plus produce probes, because without this the split array of 9 modules on 17.6 m2 (E84) cannot guarantee 21 hour operation like the Nakuru prior art.

items.feedback_item: Full-harvest and cloudy-day performance at 43C ambient breaks the staged-only design and margin is too thin for dust and derate.
items.must_change: The solution works only with staged intake of 250 kg per day needing 6.25 kWh pull-down (E28) from mass times 3.6 times 25 divided by 3600, whereas full 1000 kg loaded warm at once needs 25 kWh pull-down (E26) plus about 7.5 kWh steady thermal in one day or about 32.5 kWh thermal which cannot be met by 13.5 kWh per day electrical (E83) in one day even at COP 2. The risks and operating sequence must be changed to make the 250 kg per day over 4 days to fill 50 crates at 20 kg (E49, E77) a hard operating limit with attendant log and load shed, add condenser derate above 43C plus dust derate on 5.0 peak sun hours, and increase margin beyond 0.3 kWh per day, because otherwise extra openings or one cloud loses 5C holding.

items.feedback_item: Mass to soil pressure is correct arithmetically but the mass sum is incomplete.
items.must_change: The solution claims grown mass of 1840 kg (E87) on six pads gives pad pressure of 18.8 kPa (E89) well below 150 kPa by mass times 9.81 divided by 6 divided by 0.16, which recomputes correctly from interior volume of 8.64 m3 (E39) and envelope of 25.4 m2 (E40) with conduction of 203 W from 0.21 times 25.4 times 38 (E41), but what is actually true is the sum of 1780 kg (E66) plus 3 modules omits tube frames, monoblock, battery box, and foundation self-weight. The mass budget must be changed to list every part weight including frames and cooler and pads themselves and recompute pressure, because the factor 8 margin must be shown on the complete weight even though like a person standing at 20 to 30 kPa the result remains plausible.

items.feedback_item: Split array layout and wind anchoring and box penetrations are not fully defined as buildable structures.
items.must_change: The solution correctly finds nine-module footprint of 17.6 m2 (E84) from 9 times 1.722 times 1.134 cannot fit the 4.32 m2 roof and therefore uses split 2 on roof plus 7 on ground, with wind pressure of 375 Pa at 25 m per s from 0.5 times density times velocity squared and uplift equivalent of 673 kg from 17.6 times 375 divided by 9.81, about nine adults, so anchoring matters. The foundation and fabrication steps must be changed to draw roof gantry plus ground frame as two separate structures with no load into foam, show four screw anchor capacity exceeding uplift with pull-out calculation, resolve envelope 24 m2 in simulation versus 25.4 m2 used for conduction (E40) to the latter, and detail cooler penetration sealing and drain, because otherwise wind or leak breaks temperature holding and soil standing.

process_cause: A proposal version one was formed and all members voted ready after 3 cycles, so there is no missing proposal or unresolved blocking objection, but the meeting process allowed the vote before the deciding quantities were computed consistently, namely COP-corrected electrical load including door loss, single daily energy total, usable battery kWh with autonomy, complete mass, and anchor capacity. The thin 0.3 kWh per day margin therefore went to vote with unsettled analysis, and the process must add a recalculation cycle to close those numbers before detail design release.
summary: Sunlight to split array to battery to vapor-compression cold air over 50 vented crates near 5C in a PIR box is physically sound and matches the 1.5 tonne Nakuru prior art, but the 1-tonne staged solution is not releasable with 0.3 kWh per day margin on inconsistent thermal-electrical accounting, no battery sizing, dual door and power values, and staged-only operation vulnerable to cloud and full harvest at 43C.
